content.text: Build passes. Let me confirm nothing else in the codebase referenced the symbols I changed (removed handler names, inlined state):

Refactor complete. Here's what I did and why.

## What was concentrating complexity

`ProjectsPage` (cognitive complexity 24) mixed three unrelated concerns in one function: the **create-job form** (its own `name`/`clientId`/`status` state + `onSubmit`), the **filter controls**, and the **list**. The worst part was filter handling: three separate state vars (`showArchived`, `tagFilter`, `statusFilter`) threaded into `loadProjects` by **position**, so each handler had to re-pass the others (`loadProjects(showArchived, tagFilter, status)`, `loadProjects(next)`, `loadProjects(showArchived, tagId)`) — fragile and hard to read.

## Changes (all additive, feature-local, behavior-preserving)

1. **`projectModel.ts`** (new) — shared `Project`/`Client`/`ProjectStatus`/`STATUSES` so the form and the list agree on one shape.

2. **`ProjectForm.tsx`** (new) — the "add a job" form as a self-contained component that owns its draft state and does its own POST, matching the established sibling pattern (`ProjectTags`, `ProjectBudget`, …). This is exactly where the next change lands: adding a **code** input, its `project-form-code-error`, and duplicate-code handling now touches one small cohesive file instead of the page.

3. **`ProjectsPage.tsx`** (simplified) — collapsed the three filter states into one `Filters` object with a single `applyFilters(patch)` entry point, eliminating the positional-argument threading and folding `onFilterByTag`/`onFilterByStatus`/`onToggleArchived` into one-line handlers. Extracted a `closeIfOpen` helper. The page is now just: load data, filter, render list.

Every `data-testid`, endpoint, request body, and update semantic (optimistic append on create, `closeIfOpen` on delete/archive, identical query-param building, first-client defaulting) is preserved unchanged.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`: clean for my files (the one reported error, `import.meta.glob` in `router/routes.ts`, is pre-existing and Vite-specific — an untouched file).
- `vite build`: succeeds.

I did **not** run `bin/e2e` to a green result because the only spec in the repo (`e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts`) tests the not-yet-built job-code feature (`project-code`, `project-form-code`, `project-form-code-error`) — per the task I only restructured and did not implement it, so those assertions are expectedly still red. The refactor itself changes no existing behavior.
